Test: outside the species range

Source: R/test-docs.R
test_range.Rd

Flags records that fall outside every range polygon of their species, for example an IUCN range map. The polygons come from gazetteers = list(range = <sf>): an sf object with a species column (named like the record's species column, species, binomial or sci_name). Species without a polygon are not tested. With buffers = list(range = m), records within m metres of a polygon edge count as inside.

Fields

lon, lat, species.

Buffer

buffers = list(range = 0), in metres. The distance to an edge is measured on the ellipsoid from the closest point of the edge in a local equirectangular projection.

Custom gazetteer

required; there is no shipped range layer.

CoordinateCleaner

Equivalent to cc_iucn(); identical flags without a buffer. With a buffer CoordinateCleaner buffers the polygons with terra, so records very close to the buffer edge may differ.

See also

flag_occurrences(), flag_tests()

Other tests: test_age_equal, test_age_outlier, test_age_range_outlier, test_aohi, test_basis, test_capital, test_centroid, test_country_mismatch, test_dataset_ddmm, test_dataset_rounded, test_duplicate, test_equal, test_establishment, test_gbif_headquarters, test_gbif_issue, test_habitat, test_institution, test_invalid, test_outlier, test_sea, test_spatiotemporal_outlier, test_urban, test_zero

Examples

if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  rg <- sf::st_sf(species = "a", geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(
    rbind(c(0, 40), c(20, 40), c(20, 55), c(0, 55), c(0, 40)))), crs = 4326))
  x <- data.frame(species = c("a", "a", "b"), decimalLongitude = c(10, 30, 30),
                  decimalLatitude = 50)
  flag_occurrences(x, tests = "range", gazetteers = list(range = rg))$flag_range
}
